sentences.text: Pradhania was a modest-sized sauropodomorph that grew to about four meters in length.
A distinctive trait of this animal is a prominent horizontal crest located on the inner side of its upper jaw.
Its upper jaw held twenty teeth, a notably high count for members of its group.
These teeth were spatulate in shape and symmetrical.
The creature also possessed a large thumb claw, a feature typical of basal sauropodomorphs.
Researchers noted that Pradhania had very elongated neck vertebrae, a derived characteristic.
The genus Pradhania was first named by T. S. Kutty, Sankar Chatterjee, Peter M. Galton, and Paul Upchurch in 2007.
The genus name honors Dhuiya Pradhan, a fossil collector who worked for the Indian Statistical Institute.
The holotype fossil, ISI R265, was found in the Sinemurian-age Dharmaram Formation.
The known fossil material consists of a partial skeleton including a skull.
Evidence suggests Pradhania normally walked on its hind legs as a biped.
While originally thought to be a basal sauropodomorph, later analysis suggests Pradhania belongs to the family Massospondylidae.
A new cladistic analysis by Novas et al. in 2011 suggests Pradhania is a massospondylid rather than a basal sauropodomorph.
Pradhania lived during the Early Jurassic, approximately 196 million years ago, in what is now the Indian subcontinent.
Pradhania lived from the Hettangian to the Sinemurian stages, between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago.
